intro: This branch uses integrals to measure real things: distances, areas, volumes of solid shapes, work done by forces, and totals in probability and economics.

VI.6.01.what: The difference between how far you end up from the start (displacement) and how far you actually traveled (distance).

levels.b: Finds total distance by integrating speed.
levels.c: Finds where velocity changes sign, meaning the object turns around.
levels.d: Finds final position from a starting position and velocity.

VI.6.02.what: Integrating a rate of change gives the total change, like water flow giving the total amount added to a tank.

levels.a: Finds the total change by integrating a rate.
levels.b: Finds the amount at a later time from a starting amount.
levels.c: Handles an inflow and an outflow at the same time.
levels.d: Estimates net change from a table of rates.

VI.6.03.what: Finding the area of the region between two curves by subtracting the lower curve from the upper one.

levels.a: Integrates the top curve minus the bottom curve.
levels.b: Finds where the curves cross to get the endpoints.
levels.c: Splits the area where the top and bottom curves switch places.
levels.d: Sets up and evaluates the full area integral.

VI.6.04.what: Finding area between curves by slicing sideways instead, which is sometimes much easier.

levels.a: Integrates the right curve minus the left curve.
levels.b: Rewrites each curve with x in terms of y.
levels.c: Recognizes when slicing sideways is simpler.
levels.d: Sets up and evaluates the full area integral.

VI.6.05.what: Finding the volume of a solid by slicing it like a loaf of bread, where each slice has a known shape.

levels.a: Finds volume when each slice is a square.
levels.b: Finds volume when each slice is a semicircle.
levels.c: Finds volume when each slice is a triangle.
levels.d: Sets up the volume integral for any given slice shape.

VI.6.06.what: Finding the volume of a solid made by spinning a region around a line, by stacking thin coin-shaped disks.

levels.a: Writes the radius of each disk as a function.
levels.b: Uses pi times radius squared for each thin slice.
levels.c: Finds volumes when spinning around the horizontal axis.
levels.d: Finds volumes when spinning around the vertical axis.

VI.6.07.what: Like the disk method, but for spun solids with a hole in the middle, using ring-shaped slices called washers.

levels.a: Identifies the outer and inner radius of each ring.
levels.c: Handles spinning around lines other than the axes.
levels.d: Evaluates the integral to find the volume.

VI.6.08.what: Finding volumes of spun solids by adding up thin nested tubes, like the layers of an onion.

levels.a: Identifies the radius and height of each tube.
levels.b: Uses the tube's unrolled area, two pi times radius times height.
levels.c: Recognizes when tubes are easier than disks.
levels.d: Handles spinning around lines other than the axes.

VI.6.09.what: Finding the length of a curved path by adding up tiny straight pieces.

levels.a: Builds the length formula from Pythagoras' theorem on tiny pieces.
levels.b: Sets up the length integral for a curve.
levels.c: Evaluates it exactly or estimates it.
levels.d: Uses the sideways version with x in terms of y.

VI.6.10.what: Finding the outer surface area of a shape made by spinning a curve around a line.

levels.b: Sets up the surface area integral.
levels.d: Explores Gabriel's horn, which has finite volume but endless surface area.

VI.6.11.what: Work is force times distance. Integrals handle cases where the force changes, like stretching a spring.

levels.a: Finds work as force times distance for a constant force.
levels.b: Finds work to stretch a spring, where force grows with stretch.
levels.c: Finds work to pump liquid out of a tank.
levels.d: Finds work to lift a hanging cable or chain.

VI.6.12.what: Finding the total push of water on a wall, where the pressure grows deeper down.

levels.a: Explains that water pressure increases with depth.
levels.b: Splits the wall into thin horizontal strips.
levels.d: Finds the force on dams and underwater windows.

VI.6.13.what: Finding the balance point of a flat shape or object, where it would sit level on a pin.

levels.a: Computes moments, which measure turning effect about a line.
levels.b: Finds the balance point (centroid) of a region.
levels.c: Uses symmetry to find balance points quickly.
levels.d: Uses Pappus's theorem to find volumes from balance points.

VI.6.14.what: Using curves to describe probability, where the area under the curve over a range gives the chance of landing in it.

levels.a: Finds a probability as the area under the curve.
levels.b: Checks that the total area under the curve is one.
levels.c: Finds the average outcome using an integral.
levels.d: Works with the exponential distribution, used for waiting times.

VI.6.15.what: Using integrals in economics, such as totaling costs and measuring how much buyers and sellers gain from a sale.

levels.a: Finds a total cost or revenue from its rate per item.
levels.b: Finds consumer surplus, the benefit to buyers.
levels.c: Finds producer surplus, the benefit to sellers.
levels.d: Finds the present value of a stream of future payments.
